paper.title: AutoAgent: Evolving Cognition and Elastic Memory Orchestration for Adaptive Agents
paper.central_claim: AutoAgent: a multi-agent framework in which prompt-level cognition (tool profiles, skill library, peer profiles), contextual action selection and an Elastic Memory Orchestrator are coupled by a closed-loop cognitive evolution that updates cognition and skills without retraining, giving consistent gains in task success, tool-use efficiency and collaborative robustness over static and memory-augmented baselines.

gap.author_gap: Agents use fixed human-specified cognition, rigid workflows and inefficient context management.
gap.checked_gap: Static tool descriptions are a real, previously fixed non-weight object, but the paper gives no measurement showing misuse due to stale descriptions on its own benchmarks except the synthetic instability test.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Cited: Reflexion, Voyager, MemGPT, MemInsight, EvolveSearch (paper Sec 2, v1). Uncited by us as possible neighbours (our_inference, not verified here): tool-documentation refinement from experience and workflow/skill-memory induction; no external search was possible.
gap.residue: Peer-profile evolution and joint cognition-plus-memory loop are the claimed delta; neighbours on tool-description refinement not compared.
gap.stakes: Repeated tool misuse and context bloat; asserted, quantified only in Table 5 and Table 4.
gap.method_response: LLM-driven revision of tool/peer/skill text plus elastic memory.
gap.remaining_gap: No evidence that evolved cognition persists or transfers to later tasks outside synthetic setting; admission/rollback missing.
unresolved: Overlap between evolution tasks and evaluation tasks

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats 'task'; kept. Table 5 compares initial vs evolved cognition on the first 50 GAIA questions with no stated practice/test separation. Main-benchmark gains are not traced to retained cognition.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Single-run, author-reported results. The combined architecture beats the listed baselines on many (not all) cells under a 5-step cap. EMO on/off helps DeepSeek-R1 on GAIA/HLE. In a synthetic 50-question tool-failure setting, evolved tool descriptions raise EM. Retained improvement on later disjoint tasks, skill distillation, collaboration robustness and efficiency are not shown, and several narrative claims contradict the tables.
unresolved: Whether and how cognition evolves during the main benchmark runs (opus:O08).
LLM-judge validity; call/token cost of analyzer and EMO.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Static hand-written tool and peer descriptions are a named fixed object (son55:E001). Reflexion/Voyager/MemGPT are cited, but the claimed residual ('episodic', son55:E017) is asserted. Brittleness is shown only in the synthetic test.

M.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The chain is concrete: intention-outcome analysis → localized description edits, raw/summary/omit assembly, composite actions. It has one discriminating test (son55:E010). The attribution assumption (the failure lies in the description) and the consistency-only acceptance (son55:E004) are weak.

X.reason: Opus sides with sol. The loop exists only as prose: the selector is 'a learned or heuristic module' (opus:O07), validation is 'e.g., for consistency' (son55:E004), the evolution trigger is 'periodically' (opus:O08), and composite admission has no threshold (son55:E005). No prompts, algorithm or code are provided. The experimental section never states whether cognition, skills or peer models evolve during the reported runs. The key operations' effective conditions are missing, so this falls below anchor 2.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 1; kept, with Opus additions. Standard benchmarks are used, but GAIA/HLE pass@1 comes from an unvalidated o3-mini judge (sol:E007), and HLE is described two different ways (son55:E014). The narrative contradicts the tables in at least four places: DeepSeek-R1 GAIA 48.5 vs 52.1 and HLE 15.2 vs 28.2 (son55:E012, son55:E013), 2Wiki 'SOTA under both metrics' false on both (opus:O02), and Qwen3-30B HLE 'best' false (opus:O06). The RAG backbone is unstated. The tables themselves are not refuted, so 1, not 0.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. Four ablations are announced (son55:E011) and two are reported. EMO on/off (one backbone, two benchmarks; son55:E008) concerns per-task context management, not the retained cognition. The only evolved-vs-initial test is a synthetic 50% failure injection on 50 questions (son55:E009, son55:E010). Main-table gains are not attributed to self-evolution, skill distillation or collaboration, and the analyzer/EMO calls are uncounted against step-capped baselines (opus:O10; A2 also E.cost). sol's 2 credits two partial tests for the whole system claim.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats not_reported; re-checked. No practice/evaluation split, task order, frozen-cognition test or overlap statement exists for Table 5 or the main benchmarks (full text, no appendix).

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder). Some n are given (first 50 GAIA, HLE-500) and negative cells appear (Musique, ALFWorld DeepSeek-R1). Every result is a single run with no uncertainty (son55:E006).

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. Only caps are given: 5 steps, 1024 generation tokens per call, temperature 0.7 (son55:E007, opus:O10). Caps are design parameters, not cost evidence (precedents r02a 2410.08197, r10b 2602.02369). They also do not bound the analyzer, summariser or selector calls. The promised 'average step efficiency' is never reported (opus:O09), and the token-reduction claim has no figure (son55:E015). Precedent r04a 2504.00587 (efficiency claimed, matched agent count only) → 0.
